Every mammal has a four-chambered heart..why: Stated explicitly (88 + 35 exact sentences in two wordings, 1,813 co-occurrences) and in Wikipedia's Mammal article. Rated unlikely rather than very_unlikely: less frequent than the other rules, and a model may also reach it from the human heart's four chambers. Rules are stored, not derived: no subclass chain gives it.

sources.note: Approximate. Weak by-name storage for dolphins: sampled hits include a FAQ asking how many chambers dolphins' hearts have, and mammal feature lists.

sources.quote: The mammalian heart has four chambers, two upper atria, the receiving chambers, and two lower ventricles, the discharging chambers.

notes: Delete mirror of biology-replace-0007: the rule is removed. New members become not known (the rule was the only route); well-known members keep their value where it was stored by name and become not known where it was reached through the rule. Membership no longer needs to give way, since nothing clashes. Verifier: the dolphin's by-name storage is weak (no exact sentence; 'dolphins AND four-chambered heart' 48, mostly FAQ and list text), so its by-name world is the less likely one; it is kept as lopsided (Decision 4). Alternatives checked were no better ('bats AND four-chambered heart' 0; platypus hits are mammal feature lists, not the platypus).
